explain.say: Her prologue begins: Experience, though noon auctoritee. Even without any authority, she says, experience is enough for me. Meet Alisoun, the Wife of Bath, a cloth-maker who has married five times and been to Jerusalem three times. The panels show her life.

explain.say: Look at the third panel. Her fifth husband, Jankyn, reads aloud from a book about wicked wives. She tears out pages, he strikes her so hard she goes deaf in one ear, and in the end he gives her control. A gentle warning: this is domestic violence. Why tear the book, of all things?

explain.say: Her tale is set in King Arthur's day, and it starts with a crime: a knight attacks a young woman. The queen spares his life if, within a year, he can find what women most desire. Watch his panels. Can you guess the answer before he finds it?

explain.say: An old woman gives him the answer: sovereignty, to have mastery. In return he must marry her. Then she offers a choice: ugly and faithful, or beautiful and perhaps unfaithful. Look at the last panel. He lets her choose, and she becomes both fair and true. What changed his mind?

explain.say: So is Alisoun a feminist voice? On the left, she talks back to male authority. On the right, she is built from the very anti-woman books she attacks, by a male poet. Critics still argue. Brilliant work. Exam tip: quote her own words about experience. Challenge: decide which side you are on.

faq.q: What does the Wife of Bath say about experience and authority?
faq.a: She opens by saying her own experience of marriage is enough to speak on it, even without the authority of learned books, which were written by men who distrusted women.
asks: Experience versus authority in the Wife of Bath

faq.q: What do women most desire in the Wife of Bath’s Tale?
faq.a: Sovereignty: to have mastery over their husbands and their own lives. The old woman gives the knight this answer, and it saves his life.
asks: What is the answer to the riddle in the Wife of Bath's Tale?

faq.a: A folk-tale figure: an ugly old woman who is transformed into a beautiful one when a man treats her rightly. Gower's Tale of Florent uses the same pattern.

faq.q: Is the Wife of Bath a feminist character?
faq.a: Critics disagree. Some see her as a proto-feminist who challenges male authority; others see a comic stereotype built from medieval anti-feminist writing. Many say she is both.
asks: Is the Wife of Bath a proto-feminist?

faq.a: Jankyn reads her stories of wicked wives. She tears pages out, he hits her and deafens her in one ear, and afterwards he burns the book and gives her control of the household.
asks: Why does the Wife of Bath tear the book?

facts: The Wife of Bath says she has had five husbands at the church door.
Her tale uses the loathly lady pattern, also found in John Gower's Tale of Florent.
Her prologue is longer than her tale.
